# Benchmarking and Performance Evaluation

CS performance evaluation is a discipline of its own [@jain1991art; @georges2007rigorous].

## Warm-Up

JITs, caches, branch predictors, and TLBs all learn. Discard early iterations or report cold vs. steady state.

## Geometric Mean for Speedup

```r
speedups <- c(1.20, 0.95, 1.45, 1.10, 0.80, 1.30)
exp(mean(log(speedups)))
```

## Reporting Distributions

Show violin plots or CDFs, especially for tail latency.

## Worked Example

```r
library(dplyr); library(ggplot2); library(boot)

set.seed(7)
n <- 30
df <- data.frame(
  bench  = rep(paste0("b", 1:10), each = 2 * n),
  system = rep(rep(c("base", "new"), each = n), times = 10),
  time   = c(replicate(10, c(rlnorm(n, log(100), 0.15),
                              rlnorm(n, log( 88), 0.15))))
)

per_bench <- df |>
  group_by(bench, system) |>
  summarise(med = median(time), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = system, values_from = med) |>
  mutate(speedup = base / new)

wilcox.test(log(per_bench$base), log(per_bench$new), paired = TRUE)

gm <- function(d, i) exp(mean(log(d[i])))
b <- boot(per_bench$speedup, gm, R = 5000)
boot.ci(b, type = "bca")
```

## Beware of

- Reporting only the mean of a heavy-tailed distribution.
- Comparing across heterogeneous hardware.
- Cherry-picking benchmark subsets.
- Inferring causation from a single configuration change without A/B switch-back.
